# Verwaltung

> The firm's administration console in the Platform, where an administrator manages people and their roles (the role builder's Rollen page, with what each role may read), and a second person confirms guarded actions; the console's blueprint and role gates, on which the access pages (L2-PLATFORM-ACCESS) hang.

| Kind | code |
| Owner | `ROLE-ENGINE-OWNER` |
| Level | 2 |
| Parent | `L1-WORKSPACE` |

## Purpose

### Responsible for

| Id | Statement | Code |
|---|---|---|
| `L2-PLATFORM-ADMIN/R-1` | People (A-01, A-02): create, deactivate and activate an account (never the last active administrator), reset a password, sign a person out everywhere, set a person's roles (every role of the Rollen page, by name; her roles become exactly the checked ones, RB-4), and set a person's access groups. | `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/admin.py`; `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/templates/admin_people.html`; `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/static/js/admin_people.js` |
| `L2-PLATFORM-ADMIN/R-3` | Approvals: a guarded action (a document's access groups, a folder rule, erasing the corpus) is queued for a second person, who confirms or rejects it; an administrator acting alone is recorded as a bypass, and only an administrator switches the bypass. | `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/admin_approvals.py`; `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/guarded.py`; `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/templates/admin_approvals.html` |
| `L2-PLATFORM-ADMIN/R-4` | The console's one blueprint and its role gates, on which the other console pages (Zugriffsgruppen and Dokumente of L2-PLATFORM-ACCESS, Ingestion, Dokumentfelder, System's checks) are mounted, and the console's stylesheet. The console draws no menu of its own - its pages are the entries of the navigation's area Verwaltung, which the shell draws; each page names itself to the navigation. | `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/admin.py`; `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/static/css/admin.css` |
| `L2-PLATFORM-ADMIN/R-5` | Roles (role builder RB-3, RB-4): the Rollen page shows each role (its functions in words, what it may read, its people) and lets an administrator create, rename and delete a role of the firm's own, change a role's functions and people, and link Administration and Mitglied to their Core groups. The Core is written first and only on an administrator's form: a new role's group before the role, a rename before the role, deleting goes members, Core group, role. Every change writes its audit row by id in the same transaction, and the last active administrator keeps Administration. | `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/admin_roles.py`; `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/templates/admin_roles.html` |
| `L2-PLATFORM-ADMIN/R-6` | Agents (RB-6, RB-7): the page Agenten lists every agent (the Knovas Assistent and the external agents) with whom it acts for, its id (Knovas binds the gateway key to it) and its roles; registers an external agent for an active person or on its own, and revokes one; on a role, adds and removes an agent, the assistant included, never into Administration (the agent rows and «+ Agent hinzufügen» under «Mitglieder» of the Rollen page). After each change is committed it hands that agent's claims to the Core's gateway at once, behind the switch agents.core_gateway; a Core that refuses never breaks the page. | `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/admin_agents.py`; `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/templates/admin_agents.html` |
| `L2-PLATFORM-ADMIN/R-7` | A role's data (RB-5): the part «Darf lesen» of the Rollen page shows the folder rules naming the role's Core group and the documents whose own rights name it, read from the Core on every page (no copy kept), with «wirkt mit «Ein»» until the client reports the tenant as brokered; adds and removes a source, folder or document after a dry run of who gains and loses sight, through the four-eyes path acl_change, planned again when carried out and only by an administrator; lets a role adopt an existing Core group (FU-45) and moves people's direct group grants into roles without changing anybody's sight (FU-41). | `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/admin_role_data.py`; `KnovasPlatform/components/docbridge_integration/src/web_interface/templates/admin_roles.html` |

### Not responsible for

- Accounts, roles, sessions, the audit log and the approval queue's storage; the Platform's identity package (src/identity) keeps them (the roles in identity/roles.py, RB-1).
- Whether a role's data hide anything: the Core enforces folder rules and document rights for the Platform's claims only under brokered (CR-R1, CR-R2; a new rule over documents already read in, CR-R3); switching enforcement is RB-9 and PMVP-42.
- The access groups, the folder rules and the documents with their access groups (A-03, A-04); L2-PLATFORM-ACCESS, whose routes hang on this blueprint and its gate.
- Whether a person may read a document; the Brain decides, per customer, where enforcement is on.
- The console's Ingestion and Dokumentfelder pages and System's checks (admin_ingestion.py, admin_doc_fields.py, admin_system.py); they are mounted on this blueprint and have no card yet.
- «Was sieht …?» and the enforcement posture; today they are the Builder's (access window), and PMVP-41 and PMVP-42 bring them here.

### Terms

- guarded action (an action a second person must confirm: a document's access groups, a folder rule, erasing the corpus, an ingestion profile)
- bypass (an administrator acting alone on a guarded action, recorded as approval.bypassed)
- dry run (Probelauf: what a change of a role's data, an adopted group or the move of direct grants would do, and who would gain or lose sight under «Ein»; it writes nothing)

| `EXT-BRAIN-API` | `access-routes` | `EXT-BRAIN-API/access-routes/P-1` | through the Platform's own client on the Platform's certificate (knovas_client, passed in by the app as client_factory): the access groups, for the people page's hint on members of the tenant's administrator group at Knovas; and the Rollen page's group calls on an administrator's form (create, rename and delete a role's group, read the tenant's administrator group for Administration); a role's data (RB-5): the groups, folder rules, documents and a document's access read on every Rollen page and dry run, and on an administrator's form or a confirmed request one folder-rule or document-access write (create, update or delete a folder rule, set a document's access) and a role's previous group deleted after an adopt; never with acting_as | HTTPS with mTLS |
| `L2-BRAIN-BUILDER` |  |  | imported by admin_role_data.py (RB-5): builder.access.Tree, the tenant's group tree as the Brain returns it, for the dry runs' "a group above it reads it too" (the Core's reader closure); read only, for the page | in-process call |
| `EXT-MCP-GATEWAY` | `agent-claims-put`; `agent-claims-delete` | `EXT-MCP-GATEWAY/agent-claims-put/P-1`; `EXT-MCP-GATEWAY/agent-claims-delete/P-1` | after an agent page's change is committed, through app.extensions["agents"]["deliver"] (identity/agent_delivery.py, no card) and the Platform's own client on the Platform's certificate, without a person's assertion: the agent's pool of 20 claims, or its drop; only while agents.core_gateway is on | HTTPS with mTLS |

## To review

| At | Why |
|---|---|
| `/owner` | Proposed owner, as for every card in this repository; one role per component is confirmed by a person (Software Map K4). |
| `/status` | Live or planned is not read from the code; the console is on main and runs where the Platform runs. |
| `/responsible_for` | PMVP-11 removed the row of tabs (templates/\_admin_tabs.html): one navigation. Who sees which entry is no longer a condition in a console template; the web app reads it from the gates this blueprint puts on its routes (app.py, \_admin_pages; the shell's card): each gate (\_require_roles) puts the set of roles it checks on the view it returns, as allowed_roles, and the web app reads that attribute. No gate's check changed. admin.css still holds the rules of the removed tabs (.admin .tabs) and rules that restyle the old navigation on the console's pages (.admin-page .app-sidebar and below); the shell's shell.css outranks the second group. PMVP-40 left both: neither styles a page of its own, and tests/test_shell_nav_styles.py reads the second group. |
| `/responsible_for` | PMVP-40 (2026-11-21): the people page is one column of the shared page parts (\_parts.html); the details of a person open in the panel below the list, which admin_people.js switches as before. Roles are shown in plain words (A-02), a table in the template. Marks only for exceptions: deactivated, locked and a pending password change carry a tag, an active account none. The rules of admin.css the page no longer uses are removed and listed in work order PMVP-40; .role-chip and .document-status stay in one rule only because tests/test_shell_tokens.py names them. |
| `L2-PLATFORM-ADMIN/R-1` | RB-4 (2026-11-21) replaced the two boxes of keys (PMVP-40) and the key form of RB-1/RB-2: POST /admin/people/roles takes role ids (role_id) and makes the person's roles exactly the checked ones; the page offers every role of list_roles() by name, so a new installation shows Administration and Mitglied and no key anywhere. A Builder function comes from a role the page shows, so saving as drawn keeps it. Deactivating holds Administration's row and counts inside it (RoleStore.check_deactivation; coordinator's amendment F3), so a deactivation and a removal from Administration at once never leave it without an active person. No gate changed; ASSIGNABLE_ROLES stays for the tests that name it. |
| `L2-PLATFORM-ADMIN/R-5` | RB-3, RB-4 (work order docs/platform-mvp/work-orders/RB-3-4.md): the routes are attached by attach_role_routes with the console's require_admin, as attach_document_routes is. A Core group the request created and could not use is deleted again and the audit log names it (role.core_group_abandoned); a Core group id is never logged (a tenant may choose a speaking one). Rule 1 (no role gives more than its creator holds) is identity/roles.py grantable, which refuses nobody while admin is one coarse function (RB-10 narrows it there). |
| `/source_paths` | The work order's scope: the people page and the approvals PMVP-40 to PMVP-42 change. guarded.py is here because only console modules use it (admin_documents.py, admin_ingestion.py). admin.css is the stylesheet of every console page, those without a card too. PMVP-40 split the access groups, folder rules and documents (admin_documents.py, their two templates and admin_documents.js) into L2-PLATFORM-ACCESS: together the card was over its context budget, the code alone (16,724 tokens) over 16,000 (FU-17). The other console modules (admin_ingestion.py, admin_doc_fields.py, admin_system.py) and their pages stay outside (boundaries.yaml, not_carded); their domain is open (DEC-0083 names the Admin pages, not each console module): the project that cards them decides. |

Every other line of these routes (what they promise, their limits) has no source in § 7: PMVP-40 to PMVP-42 write them with their page tests (A-01 to A-06). Since PMVP-40 every route's N-1 has live tests in tests/test_web_admin_gates.py: the view the app registered lets in admin alone (allowed_roles); every other role the console gives (approver, ingestion_manager, member, experimenter, experiments_manager) and an account with no role get 403 and nothing runs; an administrator gets 200.
